title: Gog and Magog
lead: Magog first appears as a son of Japheth in the table of nations (Genesis 10:2). Ezekiel 38–39 makes "Gog, of the land of Magog" the leader of a last great attack on God's people, and Revelation 20:8 turns Gog and Magog into the nations gathered for the final battle. Their identity has been argued over for two thousand years. Ezekiel 38:2 can be read two ways in Hebrew: "Gog, ... chief leader of Meshech and Tubal" (nesi' rosh, with rosh as the word "chief") or "leader of Rosh, Meshech and Tubal" (with Rosh as a place or people). The identification of Gog with Russia rests on the second reading, together with the sound of the name, and is not accepted by most scholars.
